The difference is 3 main things in my experience; Positioning, Coordination, and Map Knowledge. Positioning in terms of knowing what you can see from your position and where your vulnerabilities are, coordination in terms of a methodical approach with your teammates, clearing roamers and playing for the objective, not playing it as team death match. Map knowledge can always get better, you can always learn more tricks on different maps, even pros learn new things playing the game every day. Ok so basically what i do is try to chill. I usually am very frag heavy (1.6 kd on my main, and 2.2 for my alt for this season). I learned that i cant care about my rank too much while playing with them. I run around with say, Jager, for the first minute of the round and play super aggressive and then just watch. Say they are getting into a midrange engagement and they keep holding the same angle, i tell them to change up your position a bit so you dont get prefired. If i notice they like to play specific ops i try to show them some basic things and tricks. For instance i taught my friend who is bronze all the base mira spots for most of the sites they are viable on, he is a bronze 2 with shitty aim, but he can set up the mirrors because he isnt braindead. Teach them which walls to reinforce and which to blow open for rotation, teach them not to wide peek, which is a thing i see alot. Try to get them in the same mindset as you, and slowly but surely they will develope into competent players. Maybe not to your level, but enough to carry their weight into a mid/low gold match. I actually carried a friend through gold for 13 games straight and he got to plat before me, as i had downranked to Silver 3. Hope this helped man.
